title: Model Selection Dashboard
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Train polynomial models of different degrees, compare their cross-validation scores, declare a winner, and only then unlock the test set to check your choice.

educational.topic: Model selection and comparison with cross-validation
learningObjectives: Students will be able to select a model from several candidates using cross-validation scores and their variability, and justify the choice before confirming it on held-out test data.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Guided decision-making with the test set withheld until the choice is made
keyQuestions: Why does Train R² never go down when the degree goes up?
Two models have nearly the same CV mean. What else should decide between them?
Why does the dashboard close the comparison once the test scores are shown?
commonMisconceptions: The model with the highest Train R² is the best model (Train R² rises with every added degree, even when the model is fitting noise).
The model with the highest CV mean is always the right choice (differences smaller than the standard deviation are not reliable, so a simpler model that scores about the same is often preferred).
It is fine to pick the model with the best test score (the test set then becomes part of training, and its score is no longer an honest estimate).
R-squared is always between 0 and 1 (on data the model was not fit to, it is negative whenever the model predicts worse than the mean of those points).
assessmentOpportunities: Given a table of five models with Train R², CV mean, and CV standard deviation, students choose a model, justify the choice in terms of CV mean, variability, and simplicity, and explain why the test set was not used to make the choice.
